how-it-works.headline: Three steps. Lift this week.
how-it-works.subheadline: We've never asked anyone to fill out a 14-page intake form, and we never will.

steps.title: 1. Book a tour
steps.description: Stop by any weekday for a 20-minute walkthrough. Meet a coach. See if the room feels right. No sales pitch.

steps.title: 2. Take the free week
steps.description: Five days, any classes, any time. We'll match you to a coach for your first session and give you the keys to the schedule.

steps.title: 3. Pick a plan
steps.description: Three monthly options, no contracts, pause any time. Pick what fits and start the work.

testimonials-grid.subheadline: Real members. Real names. Real lifts.

items.quote: I tried four gyms in this part of the city. Iron Forge is the only one where the coaches actually watch the lifts and call out cues. I'm 38 and lifting better than I did at 25.
items.author: Maya Patel

items.quote: The community is the whole thing. Five mornings a week with the same dozen people, watching each other PR — that's what I pay for.

items.quote: I had a serious back injury in 2022. The Iron Forge coaches built me a 6-month return plan with my PT. I'm back to deadlifting bodyweight × 2. I'd never have gotten there at a Globo gym.

features-grid.headline: Six ways to train at Iron Forge
features-grid.subheadline: Every class is capped at 12 with two coaches on the floor. Pick a format, build a habit, get strong.

features.title: Strength · 60 min
features.description: Linear-progression barbell work. Squat, bench, deadlift, press, in 4-week blocks with a percentage-based template.

features.title: Engine · 45 min
features.description: Conditioning built around an erg, a sled, and a kettlebell. Aerobic base by Tuesday, threshold work by Friday.

features.title: Olympic Lifts · 75 min
features.description: Snatch and clean & jerk technical work. Three coaches on the floor for this one. Bring your knee sleeves.

features.title: Beginner Foundations · 60 min
features.description: Twelve-week onramp for new lifters. By the end you've squatted, benched, deadlifted, and pressed under load.

features.title: Mobility · 30 min
features.description: Joint health and breath work. Tuesday and Saturday mornings. The class your future self thanks you for.

features.title: Open Gym
features.description: Run your own program with a coach available for cues. Members get unlimited open-gym access on all plans.

faq.headline: Questions before joining
faq.subheadline: If your situation isn't here, email hello@ironforge.gym — a human replies same-day.

items.question: I've never lifted with a barbell. Will I survive?
items.answer: Yes — start with Beginner Foundations. Twelve weeks, two classes a week, structured progression. By week 4 you'll be doing all four lifts. By week 12 you'll be ready for any class.

items.question: Do I need to bring my own equipment?
items.answer: No. Belts, sleeves, straps, chalk — all here. If you have your own shoes, bring them; otherwise borrow a pair until you decide what feels right.

items.question: What if I get injured?
items.answer: We work with three PTs in the neighborhood and have built return-to-lift plans with all of them. If you're rehabbing, tell your coach — we modify, we don't push through.

items.question: Can I pause my membership?
items.answer: Up to 60 days per year, no questions asked. Travel, injury, life — just message and we pause. You don't lose your spot.

items.question: Are there annual contracts?
items.answer: No. Month-to-month, cancel any time from your account. We'd rather you stay because we're good than because you're locked in.

items.question: Is this a CrossFit gym?
items.answer: No. We share some lineage but our programming is more focused: classical strength training plus aerobic conditioning, no high-rep Olympic lifts under fatigue. Quieter, more technical, fewer screams.
